note.note:
Action Plan:
1. Arrange an urgent neurology referral for suspected demyelinating disease (e.g., multiple sclerosis); request MRI brain ± cervical spine and formal neurological examination.  
2. Advise patient to attend Emergency Department (A&E) immediately if she develops new or worsening neurological symptoms (e.g., weakness in legs, persistent or worsening visual loss, severe headache, vomiting, seizures).  
3. No new medications started; continue ibuprofen as needed for musculoskeletal pain (dose/route/frequency not documented).  
4. Recommend temporarily stopping boxing and other strenuous upper-limb activities until specialist review.  
5. Schedule GP follow-up after neurology assessment to discuss results and next steps.  
6. Verbal consent from patient has been obtained before using transcription software.

Subjective:
• 46-year-old right-handed woman presents with progressive numbness and tingling of left arm for ~2 weeks, beginning after starting a boxing class.  
  – Distribution: palmar aspect of 2nd–4th fingers, extending up forearm; intermittent shoulder discomfort with movement.  
  – Symptoms worsening; not relieved by massage, warm baths, or ibuprofen.  
  – Associated subjective weakness (difficulty playing piano; occasional object-dropping).  
• One episode of transient loss of part of visual field in left eye (~20 min, a few weeks ago).  
• Occasional “fatigue-type” headaches; no seizures, no lower-limb symptoms, no neck pain.  
• Past viral illness (flu-like) one month prior.  
Past Medical History: None significant.  
Surgeries: Not mentioned.  
Medications: Ibuprofen PRN; Vitamin D; iron supplement (infrequent); Melatonin PRN (all dose/route/frequency not documented).  
Allergies: Not documented.  
Family History: Father – hypothyroidism & unspecified autoimmune disease. Mother – type 2 diabetes, hypertension, hyperlipidaemia.  
Social History: Physically active; recently started boxing; occasional binge alcohol; no data on smoking or drug use.

Objective:
(Tele-consultation – no in-person exam)  
• No vitals recorded.  
• No formal neurological examination documented.  
• No investigations to date.

Assessment & Plan:

1. Left arm numbness/weakness  
   – Assessment / likely diagnosis: Suspected demyelinating disease (Multiple sclerosis) – DDx item “Multiple sclerosis” (Medium).  
   – Differential diagnosis:  
     • Cervical radiculopathy (C7) – DDx (Medium-High); supporting boxing-related strain, conflict noted: patient denies neck pain.  
     • Median nerve entrapment – DDx (Medium).  
     • Transient ischaemic attack/minor stroke – DDx (Low-Medium).  
   – Investigations planned: Urgent MRI brain ± cervical spine; full neurological assessment; baseline bloods (FBC, U&E, B12, thyroid profile).  
   – Treatment: None yet; symptom control with OTC ibuprofen; defer disease-specific therapy pending diagnosis.  
   – Referral: Urgent neurology referral.

2. Transient left-eye visual disturbance  
   – Assessment / likely diagnosis: Possible optic neuritis (part of demyelinating process).  
   – Differential diagnosis:  
     • Amaurosis fugax (TIA) – DDx “Transient ischaemic attack” (Low-Medium).  
     • Migraine aura without headache (not listed in DDx but clinically plausible; included for completeness).  
   – Investigations planned: Included in MRI brain; consider ophthalmology assessment if symptoms recur.  
   – Treatment: As per neurology recommendations once diagnosis confirmed.  
   – Referral: Covered by neurology referral; advise patient to seek urgent care if visual symptoms recur or persist.

Quality checks:
• Missing but expected: allergies, smoking status, vitals, objective neurological examination.  
• Internal conflicts: DDx favours cervical radiculopathy but patient reports no neck pain (conflict noted).  
• Transcript quality: Clear; minor conversational digressions, no inaudible sections.
